post.summary: Watchdog: alert if audit log rotation is stale
post.description: Background maintenance: checks that the earliest row in the active audit DB is not older than ~26 hours (seal should have rotated sooner). Invoked by the `checkAuditLogRotation` cron schedule and manually by site admins. Empty active DB or age within threshold → 200 with `auditRotationStatus`. Stale rotation → 500 so the job retries then goes `dead` and is visible in the jobs admin UI. Empty body — no client fields.

schema.description: Empty JSON object. Staleness threshold is fixed server-side; no client fields.

200.description: Rotation is healthy: active DB is empty or the earliest row age is within the staleness threshold.

401.description: Unauthorized - missing or invalid auth headers, or not logged in.

403.description: Forbidden - caller is not a site admin.

500.description: Watchdog tripped: earliest active audit row is older than the staleness threshold (~26h). Job queue treats this as retryable until `dead`.

audit-rotation-status.description: Outcome of one audit-rotation watchdog check when the active audit DB is empty or the earliest row is within the staleness threshold. Unhealthy (stale) checks do not use this schema — they return HTTP 500.

healthy.description: Always `true` on 200. Present so clients can distinguish a successful check without relying solely on HTTP status.

empty.description: `true` when the active audit DB has no rows (nothing to age-check). `false` when at least one row exists and its age is within threshold.

earliest_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the oldest row in the active audit DB (`headAt`). `null` when `empty` is true.

age_ms.description: Milliseconds between `earliest_at` and the check time. `null` when `empty` is true. Always ≤ `threshold_ms` on a healthy response.

threshold_ms.description: Staleness threshold in milliseconds (26 hours). An `age_ms` above this value causes the operation to return 500 instead of this body.

code.description: A short, machine-readable error code, for when HTTP status codes are not sufficient.

message.description: A human-readable description of the error.
message.example: The requested resource could not be found.

session.name: ory_kratos_session
session.description: Signed-in SAF user (Kratos browser session; internal job calls present the same identity via a signed assertion, which is not modeled here). Scopes: `email-verified`, `mfa`, `site-admin` (implies email-verified + mfa).
